title: Russia and North Korea Open First-Ever Road Bridge Across Shared Border
detail: Russia and North Korea opened their first purpose-built road bridge across the Tumen River on September 7, 2026, linking North Korea's Rason with Russia's Khasan. The 1-kilometer, two-lane bridge — named after Soviet officer Yakov Novichenko, credited with shielding Kim Il-sung from a 1946 assassination attempt — can process up to 300 vehicles a day through a newly built border crossing point. Trucks from each country drove toward each other across the span in a simultaneous inauguration ceremony, with Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and North Korean Premier Pak Thae Song attending via video link; Mishustin said the crossing would boost bilateral trade, while Pak called it 'a significant event adding a new dynamic movement to the overall bilateral cooperation.' The bridge was agreed under the June 2024 Kim-Putin strategic partnership treaty and follows commercial satellite imagery in late August showing the DPRK approach nearly complete.

media.caption: Trucks cross the new Tumen River road bridge linking Russia's Khasan and North Korea's Rason, Sept 7, 2026
